title: Top-account escalation SLA derivation and automated sprint slotting
creator: Elaine Soto
description: Define and implement an objective derivation for SLA windows placed on top-account escalation requests and map those SLAs into automated sprint 'slots' that feed the product roadmap planner. The aim is to reduce ad-hoc escalations, ensure predictable delivery expectations with customers, and make trade-offs across cycles explicit and auditable. This ticket covers the scoring rules, capacity mapping algorithm, UI contract for the intake form, and the initial automation prototype that emits candidate sprint placement recommendations to PMs and Eng leads.
background: We receive frequent high-touch escalations from strategic accounts that request expedited delivery or roadmap commitments. Current handling is manual: CS/AM flags a request, an ad-hoc discussion with PM/Eng determines feasibility, and timelines are promised with variable rigor. This creates risk: over-committing, opaque prioritization, and last-minute scope rework. Several existing playbooks reference similar concepts (fastpass lanes, commitment windows) but lack a single deterministic derivation that ties customer signals to engineering capacity and cycle calendars.
proposed_solution: 1) Create a composite Escalation SLA Score composed of weighted signals: revenue runway (30%), customer risk (20%), product fit delta (15%), number of affected customers (10%), legal/compliance urgency (15%), and exec sponsorship strength (10%). Each signal has a defined scale (0-10) and guidance for raters. 2) Translate an SLA Score into a canonical delivery window (Hot: 1 cycle, Warm: 2 cycles, Standard: 3+ cycles) and a slot size (small/medium/large) determined by a capped effort estimate distribution. 3) Implement an automated slotting algorithm in the roadmap planner: match SLA-derived slots to available engineering capacity per cycle using an 'accordion' allocator that reserves fractional capacity across cycles while minimizing disruption to already-booked work. 4) Surface recommendations in the Console intake UI with explicit trade-offs (expected block duration, estimated engineering points, confidence level, and fallback model). 5) Provide an audit trail and expirable SLA token that, if accepted, creates a flagged roadmap item with an enforced follow-up cadence and alerting if commitments slide.
success_metrics: Time-to-decision on escalations reduced from median 6 business days to <= 3 business days
Percentage of top-account escalation promises delivered within agreed SLA >= 85% at 90-day horizon
Reduction in off-plan scope incidents attributed to escalations by 40% over two quarters
PM/Eng satisfaction with slot suggestions (survey) >= 4/5 after pilot
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): Q2 pilot for 3 named strategic accounts. Build scoring rubric, intake UI changes, slotting prototype, and run manual validation with PM + Eng for each recommendation (no auto-apply). Phase 2 (automation): After 4-week pilot evaluation, enable auto-suggest in Console with acceptance flow. Phase 3 (scale): Integrate with Dedicated capacity views and enforce SLA tokens for escalations tied to legal/contractual obligations. Target full rollout in roadmap-2026.04 release with opt-in by Sales/CS teams.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect signal weighting leads to misprioritization. Mitigation: Start with conservative weights, periodic calibration using historical escalations, and require cross-functional sign-off for Hot classifications. Risk: Engineering capacity model mismatch. Mitigation: Use a conservative fractional reservation and expose 'accordion' elasticity knobs to Eng leads. Risk: Customer dissatisfaction if SLA expectations slip. Mitigation: Create explicit fallback messaging and an escalation communications playbook; automatically notify customer success when a flagged item moves out of slot.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric documented and reviewed by PM, Sales, and CS (review notes captured)
Prototype slotting algorithm produces consistent recommendations for 10 historical escalation examples (documented)
Intake UI updated to capture required signals and surface recommended SLA window and slot size
Roadmap planner accepts and stores SLA tokens and emits a human-readable audit trail
Pilot run with 3 accounts completed and feedback loop established for weight adjustments
notes: Keep the initial UX lightweight—we want PMs to validate recommendations, not be forced. Coordinate with Analytics for a small dataset of historical escalations to help seed weights. Align with Legal on any promise wording when SLAs are surfaced to customers.
